quiz_met5:1.q: A patient cannot deliver bile salts to the small intestine. Which step of dietary fat handling is directly lost?
quiz_met5:1.r: Step 1: bile salts emulsify dietary fats in the small intestine, forming mixed micelles.

quiz_met5:2.q: In what form are absorbed dietary fatty acids exported from the intestinal mucosa to the tissues?
o: Free fatty acids on serum albumin
Free fatty acids in bile salts
quiz_met5:2.r: Steps 3 to 5: the mucosa converts fatty acids into triacylglycerols, which are incorporated into chylomicrons that move through lymph and blood to tissues.

quiz_met5:3.q: A child is born without functional apoC-II. After a fatty meal, which enzyme in the capillaries fails to be activated?
quiz_met5:3.r: Step 6: lipoprotein lipase, activated by apoC-II in the capillary, converts triacylglycerols to fatty acids and glycerol.

quiz_met5:4.q: A person moves from rest to sprinting and later to an overnight fast. Which tissue keeps relying mainly on fatty acids for energy throughout?
quiz_met5:4.r: Cardiac muscle: majority of energetic needs supplied by fatty acids under all physiological conditions.

quiz_met5:5.q: Under which condition does skeletal muscle metabolize fatty acids?
quiz_met5:5.r: Skeletal muscle metabolizes fatty acids when resting or undergoing relatively low intensity exercise.

quiz_met5:6.q: Which two hormones activate adenylyl cyclase in the adipocyte to begin mobilizing stored triacylglycerol?
quiz_met5:6.r: Epinephrine and glucagon both activate adenylyl cyclase, leading to activation of PKA.

quiz_met5:7.q: Once PKA is active in an adipocyte, which protein coating the lipid droplet does it act on so that lipases can reach the stored fat?
quiz_met5:7.r: PKA activates (phosphorylates) perilipin, freeing a fat droplet, and several lipases which cleave the fatty acids from TAG.

quiz_met5:8.q: After lipases cleave stored triacylglycerol in adipose tissue, where can the glycerol backbone travel, and for what use?
quiz_met5:8.r: The glycerol backbone can travel to the liver for gluconeogenesis.

quiz_met5:9.q: Activation of a fatty acid by fatty acyl-CoA synthetase consumes ATP. Which nucleotide is released when coenzyme A attacks the enzyme-bound intermediate?
quiz_met5:9.r: The thiol group of coenzyme A attacks the acyl-adenylate, displacing AMP and forming the thioester fatty acyl-CoA.

quiz_met5:10.q: Why must a fatty acyl group be handed to carnitine instead of entering the matrix as fatty acyl-CoA?
o: Albumin holds it in the cytosol
quiz_met5:10.r: Cells maintain separate pools of CoA in the cytoplasm and matrix, so fatty acyl-CoA cannot be directly imported into the matrix.

quiz_met5:11.q: After acylcarnitine crosses the inner mitochondrial membrane, which enzyme reattaches the fatty acyl group to coenzyme A?
quiz_met5:11.r: Carnitine acyltransferase II on the matrix side transfers the acyl group from carnitine back to CoA; once in the matrix the fatty acid is reattached to CoA.

quiz_met5:12.q: An infant with a defective OCTN2 carnitine transporter becomes hypoglycemic during a fast, yet no ketones are detected. What best explains the missing ketones?
o: Ketones are lost in the urine
quiz_met5:12.r: An OCTN2 defect decreases the ability of tissue to take up the carnitine needed to oxidize fatty acids; liver ketone output is crossed out (hypoketotic hypoglycemia, p. 807).

quiz_met5:13.q: A patient lacks the beta-oxidation enzyme that passes electrons to FAD. Which enzyme is deficient?
quiz_met5:13.r: Acyl-CoA dehydrogenase converts palmitoyl-CoA to trans-enoyl-CoA while reducing FAD to FADH2.

quiz_met5:14.q: How many NADH are produced directly by the beta-oxidation rounds that convert one palmitoyl-CoA into acetyl-CoA?
quiz_met5:14.r: Palmitoyl-CoA + 7 CoA + 7 FAD + 7 NAD+ + 7 H2O gives 8 acetyl-CoA + 7 FADH2 + 7 NADH + 7 H+.

quiz_met5:15.q: In a fasting hepatocyte, acetyl-CoA builds up faster than the citric acid cycle can accept it. Which enzyme does this directly inhibit?
quiz_met5:15.r: Acetyl-CoA 'inhibits thiolase' (p. 789); ketone bodies are made to avoid inhibition of thiolase (p. 807).

quiz_met5:16.q: During fasting, gluconeogenesis withdraws intermediates from the citric acid cycle, creating a bottleneck at its first reaction. Which intermediates are drawn off?
quiz_met5:16.r: Gluconeogenesis draws off oxaloacetate and malate from the TCA cycle, which can lead to a bottleneck at the first reaction.

quiz_met5:17.q: Releasing ketone bodies relieves the liver's acetyl-CoA buildup. What is the second function of ketone body release?
o: Raises insulin release in a fast
quiz_met5:17.r: Two functions: avoids inhibition of continued beta-oxidation by high acetyl-CoA, and shares the energy stored in the fatty acid with the extra-hepatic tissues.

quiz_met5:18.q: In a myocyte, acetoacetate is converted to acetoacetyl-CoA before being split into two acetyl-CoA. Which molecule donates the coenzyme A?
quiz_met5:18.r: In peripheral tissue mitochondria, thiophorase converts acetoacetate to acetoacetyl-CoA while succinyl-CoA becomes succinate.

quiz_met5:19.q: Hepatocytes synthesize ketone bodies, but one enzyme of ketone body breakdown is expressed only in extra-hepatic tissues. Which enzyme?
quiz_met5:19.r: Thiophorase is only expressed in extra-hepatic tissues.

quiz_met5:20.q: A healthy person on a prolonged fast makes ketone bodies but does not develop ketoacidosis. What keeps the process from running away?
quiz_met5:20.r: In a healthy fast, gluconeogenesis is shut down by the release of insulin once the normal glucose set-point is exceeded; in diabetic ketoacidosis insulin signaling is missing.

quiz_met5:21.q: When the citric acid cycle is well supplied with fuel, one of its intermediates slows glycolysis by inhibiting PFK1. Which intermediate?

quiz_met5:22.q: Which enzyme of the citric acid cycle carries out its single substrate-level phosphorylation, producing GTP?
quiz_met5:22.r: Step 5, succinyl-CoA synthetase: GDP + Pi to GTP, the one substrate-level phosphorylation (p. 797).

quiz_met5:23.q: Succinate dehydrogenase is tightly bound to the inner mitochondrial membrane. To which carrier does it pass electrons directly through its FAD?
quiz_met5:23.r: Electrons are transferred directly to Coenzyme Q via the FAD coenzyme and enter the electron transport chain.

quiz_met5:24.q: The malate dehydrogenase reaction has a strongly positive standard free energy change, yet it runs forward in the cycle. Why?
o: GTP hydrolysis is coupled to it
quiz_met5:24.r: Reaction driven forward by mass action: oxaloacetate concentration is kept very low (5 micromolar) because citrate synthase uses it.

quiz_met5:25.q: Which molecule activates both citrate synthase and isocitrate dehydrogenase?
quiz_met5:25.r: Citrate synthase is activated by ADP; isocitrate dehydrogenase is activated by Ca2+ and ADP. AMP activates only the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex.

quiz_met5:26.q: During fasting, fatty acids are abundant. Which enzyme do fatty acids inhibit, matching acetyl-CoA supply to the needs of the cycle?
quiz_met5:26.r: The pyruvate dehydrogenase complex is inhibited by ATP, acetyl-CoA, NADH and fatty acids.

quiz_met5:27.q: A cell making porphyrins and heme withdraws which citric acid cycle intermediate as the precursor?
quiz_met5:27.r: On the amphibolic slide, succinyl-CoA leads to porphyrins and heme.

quiz_met5:28.q: Which anaplerotic enzyme operates in liver and kidney and consumes ATP to form oxaloacetate?
quiz_met5:28.r: Pyruvate + bicarbonate + ATP gives oxaloacetate + ADP + Pi by pyruvate carboxylase; tissues: liver, kidney.

quiz_met5:29.q: The anaplerotic reaction catalyzed by PEP carboxykinase is listed for which tissues?
quiz_met5:29.r: Phosphoenolpyruvate + CO2 + GDP gives oxaloacetate + GTP by PEP carboxykinase; tissues: heart, skeletal muscle.

quiz_met5:30.q: Three of the four anaplerotic reactions yield oxaloacetate. Which enzyme instead yields a different cycle intermediate?
quiz_met5:30.r: Malic enzyme: pyruvate + bicarbonate + NAD(P)H gives malate + NAD(P)+; the other three reactions give oxaloacetate.

Met 5 High-Yield Tables

Met 5: Fatty Acid Catabolism and the TCA Cycle (Jones). You have never been quizzed on this lecture and marked it for a redo. Page numbers are pages of the combined PDF, where the lecture runs pp. 774 to 807. Everything is from her slides unless labeled (outside the slides).

1. Dietary fat absorption (LO 1)

Dietary fat is emulsified, digested, rebuilt into triacylglycerol and shipped in chylomicrons through lymph and blood to the tissues (p. 781).

Pathway in order (p. 781)

Step What happens Location Enzyme or molecule required
1 Dietary fats are emulsified into mixed micelles Small intestine Bile salts
2 Triacylglycerols are degraded Small intestine Intestinal lipases
3 Fatty acids and other breakdown products are taken up and converted back into triacylglycerols Intestinal mucosa
4 Triacylglycerols are incorporated, with cholesterol and apolipoproteins, into chylomicrons Intestinal mucosa Apolipoproteins
5 Chylomicrons move to the tissues Lymphatic system, then bloodstream
6 Triacylglycerols are converted to fatty acids and glycerol Capillary Lipoprotein lipase, activated by apolipoprotein C-II (apoC-II)
7 Fatty acids enter cells Myocyte or adipocyte
8 Fatty acids are oxidized as fuel or reesterified for storage Myocyte or adipocyte

Enzymes and digestive molecules (p. 781)

Molecule Type Job
Bile salts Digestive molecule Emulsify dietary fats and form mixed micelles
Intestinal lipases Enzyme Degrade triacylglycerols in the small intestine
Lipoprotein lipase Enzyme Converts chylomicron triacylglycerols to fatty acids and glycerol in the capillary
apoC-II Apolipoprotein on the chylomicron Activates lipoprotein lipase

Component Detail on the slide

Apolipoprotein C-III Labeled on the particle surface
Apolipoprotein C-II Labeled on the particle surface

Triacylglycerols and cholesteryl esters Labeled in the particle interior

Her summary line (p. 807)

Review point Page
Free fatty acids are absorbed in the intestine and incorporated as triacylglycerols into chylomicrons 807

2. Fatty acid mobilization and tissue fuel use (LO 2)

Epinephrine and glucagon make adipocytes release fatty acids, which travel on serum albumin to tissues that burn them (p. 782).

Step numbers are the circled numbers on the slide. The slide has no caption, so the wording follows its arrows.

Step What happens Location

5 Fatty acids are cleaved from triacylglycerol Adipocyte lipid droplet
6 Fatty acids leave the adipocyte and bind serum albumin Bloodstream
7 Fatty acids enter the cell through a fatty acid transporter Myocyte
8 Beta-oxidation, citric acid cycle and respiratory chain yield carbon dioxide and ATP Myocyte

3. Fatty acyl-CoA, the carnitine shuttle and beta-oxidation (LO 3)

Fatty acids are activated to fatty acyl-coenzyme A (CoA), carried into the matrix on carnitine, and cut into acetyl-CoA by beta-oxidation (p. 784).

Overall order of fatty acid oxidation (p. 784)

  1. Convert the free fatty acid to fatty acyl-CoA.
  2. Transport it into the mitochondria by the carnitine shuttle.
  3. Carry out repeated rounds of beta-oxidation.
  4. Odd-chain and unsaturated fatty acids require additional steps, which she does not show.

Three stages for a 16-carbon fatty acid (p. 784)

Stage Process What the slide shows it producing
1 Beta-oxidation 8 acetyl-CoA, plus electrons
2 Citric acid cycle 16 carbon dioxide, plus 64 electrons
3 Respiratory (electron-transfer) chain Adenosine triphosphate (ATP) from adenosine diphosphate (ADP) and phosphate, and water from oxygen

Electrons from stages 1 and 2 are carried as NADH and FADH2.

Carrier Full name Oxidized form
NADH Reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide NAD+
FADH2 Reduced flavin adenine dinucleotide FAD

Step 1 of the overall order: making fatty acyl-CoA (p. 785)

Step Enzyme What happens Standard free energy change
1 Fatty acyl-CoA synthetase ATP adenylylates the carboxylate ion, giving enzyme-bound fatty acyl-adenylate and pyrophosphate
2 Fatty acyl-CoA synthetase The thiol group of CoA attacks the acyl-adenylate, displacing adenosine monophosphate (AMP) and forming the thioester fatty acyl-CoA -15 kJ/mol for the two-step process
Side reaction Inorganic pyrophosphatase Pyrophosphate is immediately hydrolyzed to two molecules of phosphate -19 kJ/mol

Step 2 of the overall order: the carnitine shuttle (p. 786)

Step What happens Enzyme or protein Location as drawn
1 Acyl group moves from CoA to carnitine, releasing free CoA Carnitine acyltransferase I Outer mitochondrial membrane, facing the cytosol
2 Acylcarnitine enters the matrix and free carnitine returns Transporter Inner mitochondrial membrane
3 Acyl group moves from carnitine back to CoA, giving fatty acyl-CoA Carnitine acyltransferase II Matrix side of the inner membrane
Why the shuttle exists Page
Cells keep separate pools of CoA in the cytoplasm and matrix 786
Fatty acyl-CoA therefore cannot be directly imported into the matrix 786
In the cytoplasm the fatty acid is attached to carnitine 786

Once in the matrix, the fatty acid is reattached to CoA 786

4. Ketone bodies, fasting and diabetic ketoacidosis (LO 4)

The liver turns excess acetyl-coenzyme A (CoA) into ketone bodies whenever gluconeogenesis drains the cycle, and peripheral tissues burn them (p. 791).

The three ketone bodies (p. 791, 792)

Ketone body Note on the slides Page
Acetone Exhaled 792
Acetoacetate Released into blood and used by peripheral tissues 791, 792
D-beta-hydroxybutyrate Released into blood and used by peripheral tissues 791, 792

Why the liver makes ketone bodies (p. 791)

  1. Gluconeogenesis and ketone synthesis occur together.
  2. Gluconeogenesis draws off oxaloacetate and malate from the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle.
  3. This can cause a bottleneck at the first reaction of the TCA cycle.
  4. Ketone bodies are formed from the excess acetyl-CoA and released into the blood.
Function of ketone body release Page
Avoids inhibition of continued beta-oxidation by high acetyl-CoA (thiolase is the enzyme inhibited) 791, 807
Shares the energy stored in the fatty acid with the extra-hepatic tissues 791

HMG-CoA is 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA (name expansion is outside the slides).

Step Conversion Enzyme Location

5 Acetoacetate to beta-hydroxybutyrate, using reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADH) Mitochondria of liver cells
6 Acetoacetate and beta-hydroxybutyrate are released Circulation
